Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a metaproteomics analysis of ancient dental calculus. While deamidation is searched for (common in palaeoproteomics), it is used as a marker of antiquity rather than a targeted PTM enrichment workflow. No specific enrichment (like phospho or glyco) was performed.

organism: Mycobacterium leprae genome (6.6-fold), the causative agent of leprosy, recovered via shotgun sequencing of sixteenth-century human dental calculus
noncellular_sources: dental calculus (figure 1b) and a premolar tooth belonging to a female individual (SK92/N86160)
scope: The calculus were demineralized in 1 ml of 15% acetic acid overnight then spun for ten minutes, after which the supernatant was removed. The pellet was then resuspended in 2M guanidine hydrochloride solution
The pellet was physically crushed using sterile micro-pestles to ensure maximum coverage of the lysis buffer.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis was performed on a metaproteomic extract from dental calculus containing both human and M. leprae proteins. The processing involved total protein extraction from the mineralized matrix (demineralization and lysis), which corresponds to a whole cell lysate/extract scope of the material present in the calculus.
